entries.title: How do I transfer issuer-sponsored shares (SRN) to my margin loan?
entries.answer: Use the Security Transfer Form (LE044) to lodge issuer-sponsored shares held under an SRN to your Margin Loan.
steps: Section 1 (Facility Details): enter your Loan Account Name and Loan Account Number.
Section 2 (Equity Instructions): tick 'Lodge equities (shares) to the Margin Loan'.

Section 3 (Lodgement Instructions): enter your Margin Loan HIN and registered name, then tick 'Lodge Issuer Sponsored security to the Margin Loan Facility' and list the security code, SRN and number of shares.
Attach your latest issuer-sponsored holding statement for each security.
Section 5: every security owner signs and dates the form. Companies and trusts indicate the signing capacity.
Send it by mail to Leveraged, GPO Box 5388, Sydney NSW 2001, or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au.
notes: If the shares are not held in the Borrower's or a Guarantor's name, you also need an original Australian Standard Transfer Form to change ownership.
A fee may be payable when a transfer results in a change of ownership. See the fee schedule.

entries.title: How do I transfer money into my margin loan?
entries.answer: You can put money into your Loan Account by bank transfer (EFT), BPAY or direct debit from your nominated bank account. Money you deposit reduces your loan balance.
steps: EFT: transfer to the BSB and account number you were given when your margin loan was set up. This is an Adelaide Bank account used only for payments into your Loan Account.
BPAY: pay using the BPAY details for your Loan Account.
Direct debit: ask us to debit your nominated bank account. Direct debits take three business days to clear, so a debit processed on Monday is available Thursday morning.
Check the deposit has arrived by logging in to Leveraged Online.
notes: Use EFT or BPAY rather than posting a cheque, to avoid delays.

Can't find your BSB, account number or BPAY details? Call 1300 307 807 (Mon–Fri, 8:30am–5:30pm AEST/AEDT) or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au. Never send money to account details received in an unexpected email or call.
To nominate or change a bank account for direct debits, we need confirmation of the BSB, account number and account name from your bank, usually a bank statement.

entries.title: How do I transfer broker-sponsored shares (HIN) to my margin loan?
entries.answer: Use the Security Transfer Form (LE044). You can lodge a whole broker-sponsored HIN, or selected securities from it.
steps: Section 1: enter your Loan Account Name and Loan Account Number.
Section 2: tick 'Lodge equities (shares) to the Margin Loan'.
Section 3: enter your Margin Loan HIN and registered name, then choose one option:

Option A: 'Lodge following broker sponsored HIN'. This moves every holding in that HIN and keeps your existing TFN and dividend instructions. Enter the broker name, broker account number and broker HIN.
Option B: 'Transfer the following Broker Sponsored security'. List the broker details, security code and number of shares. You may need to re-nominate TFN and dividend instructions.
Section 5: every security owner signs and dates the form.
Send it by mail to Leveraged, GPO Box 5388, Sydney NSW 2001, or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au.
notes: If the shares are not held in the Borrower's or a Guarantor's name, you also need an original Australian Standard Transfer Form.

entries.title: How do I release shares from my margin loan?
entries.answer: Use the Security Transfer Form (LE044), section 4 'Release Equity from the Margin Loan'.
steps: Section 1: enter your Loan Account Name and Loan Account Number.
Section 2: tick 'Release equities from the Margin Loan'.

Section 4: enter the Margin Loan HIN and registered name, then choose to release the whole broker-sponsored HIN, all holdings to a broker-sponsored account, selected securities to broker-sponsored, or a security to issuer-sponsored (with its SRN).
Section 5: every security owner signs and dates the form.
Send it by mail or email to Leveraged.
notes: Releasing shares reduces the security behind your loan. Check your available funds and loan-to-value position first.

entries.title: How do I apply for a loan?
entries.answer: Most people apply online in one sitting. Read the PDS for the product first. You can also talk to a Business Development Manager before you start.
steps: Compare the Margin Loan, Investment Funds Multiplier and Direct Investment Loan.
Read the PDS and Product Guide for the loan you choose.
Complete the online application.
notes: The Direct Investment Loan is available to individual and joint borrowers only, not companies or trusts.
Leveraged loans are not available to self-managed superannuation funds.

entries.title: Who can apply for the Direct Investment Loan?
entries.answer: The Direct Investment Loan is available to individual and joint borrowers only. It is not available to companies, trusts or self-managed superannuation funds. Managed funds are not acceptable investments for this loan, and the maximum credit limit is $500,000.

entries.title: What can I borrow against?
entries.answer: Each loan has its own acceptable investments list showing the eligible securities and their lending ratios. Check the recent changes list too. Lists can change at any time.

entries.title: What is a margin call and what do I need to do?
entries.answer: A margin call is made when your loan balance goes above your lending value plus the buffer. This usually happens when the market value of your investments falls, which lowers your lending value.
steps: If you get a margin call you'll usually need to act within 24 hours.
Reduce the shortfall by repaying some of the loan, adding cash or acceptable investments, or selling investments.
If you don't act, Leveraged can sell investments for you.
notes: Between your lending value and the buffer limit you can't draw more funds, but no margin call is made.
Keep your margin call contact details up to date so we can reach you quickly.

entries.title: How are lending value, available funds and margin calls worked out?
entries.answer: Lending value is each holding's market value multiplied by its lending ratio, added up. Available funds are the lower of your lending value and credit limit, minus your loan balance. The 'How it works' page has worked examples and a calculator.

entries.answer: Your HIN is your Holder Identification Number that your shares are registered on. You are able to find this number under the Investments menu on Leveraged Online.

entries.title: How do I determine the LVR and price of a particular stock?

If you do not hold the stock, you can determine the LVR by referencing our Acceptable Investments Lists.
You can also access the Acceptable Investments List via Leveraged Online by clicking on Lending Ratio Search towards the bottom of the menu on the left hand side, and then selecting Acceptable Investment List.
You can also enter the ASX code in the search field under Lending Ratio Search to view the LVR as well as the current price.

entries.title: What is a Target Facility Balance?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer: A Target Facility Balance is the minimum Loan Balance requested by the Borrower and approved by the Lender that applies to the facility.

entries.title: Who can apply for a Target Facility Balance?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer: Margin Loan and Direct Investment Loan Borrowers can apply for a Target Facility Balance to apply to their facility. The option is not available on Investments Funds Multiplier facilities.

entries.title: What is a Linked Investment Account?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer:
A Linked Investment Account is a bank account opened in our name (or in our nominee’s name) for, and at the request of, the Borrower, that is linked to the facility.
In limited cases we may accept a Cash Management Trust account opened in the name of the Borrower or Guarantor as Linked Investment Account.

entries.title: What is a sweep?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer:
A sweep is an automated process via which the Linked Investment Account will be credited or debited with funds from or to the Loan Account depending on the Target Facility Balance on the margin loan facility.
A sweep from the Linked Investment Account will be dependent on funds availability and minimum balance requirement of the Linked Investment Account.
A sweep is an overnight process and can only take place on a Business Day. Transactions are reflected on the Loan Account and the Linked Investment Account the following Business Day.

entries.title: What happens if the loan balance is below the Target Facility Balance?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer:
While a Target Facility Balance applies to the facility and the Loan Balance is below the Target Facility Balance, an automated process operates so that the Borrower is taken to have:
given us a borrowing request for an amount that would result in the Loan Balance being the same as (or as close as reasonably practicable to) the Target Facility Balance; and
directed us to advance such amount to the relevant Linked Investment Account
The automated process will sweep funds from the Loan Account to the Linked Investment Account when this happens.

entries.title: What happens if the Loan Balance is above the Target Facility Balance?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer:
While a Target Facility Balance applies to the facility and the Loan Balance is above the Target Facility Balance, an automated process operates so that the Borrower is taken to have:
asked to direct debit the relevant Linked Investment Account for an amount that results the loan balance being substantially the same as (or as close as reasonably practicable to) the Target Facility Balance.
Directed us to deposit such an amount into the Loan Account.
The automated process will sweep funds from the Linked Investment Account to the Loan Account.

entries.title: What are the different Target Facility Balances I can have?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer:
a) Target Facility Balance of $0.00
If the Target Facility Balance is $0.00 then any credit balance in the Loan Account will be swept to the Linked Investment Account to bring the Loan Balance to $0.00
If the Loan Balance is greater than $0.00 (Target Facility Balance), any available balance in the Linked Investment Account will be swept to the Loan Account to reduce the Loan Balance to $0.00 or as close to $0.00 as achievable.
A Target Facility Balance of $0.00 is not available if the Borrower has a fixed rate loan.
b) Target Facility Balance equal to fixed rate loan
If the Target Facility Balance is equal to a fixed rate loan amount, then:
Any undrawn portion of the fixed rate loan will be swept to the Linked Investment Account so that the Loan Balance is equal to the fixed rate loan (Target Facility Balance).
Any available balance in the Linked Investment Account will be swept to the Loan Account to reduce the Loan Balance to an amount equal to the fixed rate loan (or as close to that amount as achievable).
c) Target Facility Balance above $0.00
A Target Facility Balance above $0.00 is set up at a specified amount requested by the Borrower and approved by the Lender. If the Loan Balance is:
Less than the agreed Target Facility Balance, then the difference will be swept from the Loan Account to the Linked Investment Account to make the Loan Balance the same as Target Facility Balance.
If the Loan Balance is greater than the Target Facility Balance, any available balance in the Linked Investment Account will be swept to the Loan Account to reduce the Loan balance to the agreed Target Facility Balance (or as close to it as achievable).

entries.title: I am a Borrower who has a Loan Balance which comprises both fixed rate and variable rate amounts. Can I sweep both the fixed and variable rate amounts?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer: Borrowers can only sweep either a variable rate or a fixed rate Loan Balance, they cannot sweep both.

entries.title: Do Borrowers have access to funds in the Linked Investment Account?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer: Borrowers will not have direct access to funds in the Linked Investment Account as it is restricted. Features such as setting up direct debits and ATM cards are not available on Linked Investment Accounts. This is because the Linked Investment Account comprises security for the loan.

entries.title: Can Borrowers withdraw funds from the Linked Investment Account?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer: The Linked Investment Account forms part of the security for the Loan Balance. Borrowers will need to contact us to withdraw funds from the Linked Investment Account.

entries.title: Is there a minimum balance required to be maintained in the Linked Investment Account?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer: Linked Investment Accounts require a certain minimum balance to be maintained in the account. Please contact us on 1300 307 807 or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au for further details.

entries.title: What interest rate is paid on a Linked Investment Account?
entries.group: FAQ: Target Facility Balance and Linked Investment Accounts
entries.answer: The interest rate will be determined by the account provider from time to time. If you would like further information on the rates, please contact us on 1300 307 807 or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au.

entries.title: How can I close my account?
entries.answer:
Please contact your Relationship Manager to close your margin loan. Your Relationship Manager will send you the relevant Account Closure form.
Alternatively, call us on 1300 307 807 or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au.
